contributor_rule_quote: AI policy: Rules for using AI tools when you contribute
notes: CONTRIBUTING.md links Moby's AI_POLICY.md (github.com/moby/.github), which asks contributors to disclose the AI tool and how much it did. AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md give agents workflow rules only. The docs host the Gordon AI assistant, which answers questions; nothing says how pages are written.
README and CONTRIBUTING.md never mention AI; no AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.

statement_quote: Most of the guides began with AI-generated first drafts through some clever prompting
notes: AWS Insights post by the head of the AWS Documentation, SDK and CLI teams, 2025-02-13, about the AWS Decision Guides. The same post says AI-generated content shown without that review 'will always be clearly labeled as such'. No public docs source: AWS archived most awsdocs repos in June 2023.

Translated pages carry an AI translation notice, e.g. docs.cloud.google.com/docs?hl=in: 'Google menggunakan teknologi AI untuk menerjemahkan konten ke dalam bahasa pilihan Anda.' Recorded, not counted: it covers translation of pages, not how the English source is written. No public docs source (no edit link; 'Send feedback' only).

statement_quote: We are optimistic about asking stakeholders to use AI to create initial drafts of documentation
notes: Cloudflare Style Guide section 'How we AI' (page last updated 2026-04-24), with prompt templates and a video workflow page that uses Gemini for scripts. The docs repo README adds: 'We may use AI tools to help us review technical documentation, pull requests and other issues submitted'. CONTRIBUTING.md is silent on AI; AGENTS.md gives agents build and style rules only.

contributor_rule_quote: These guidelines apply whether you write the change yourself or use an AI assistant.
notes: AGENTS.md is an operating guide for agents (verify before you claim, smallest change); no disclosure rule and nothing on how HashiCorp's writers use AI.
AI disclaimers on Firebase docs cover Gemini features' output, not the docs. No public docs source (no edit link).

contributor_rule_quote: When contributing with AI assistance, follow the Ansible Community Policy for AI-Assisted Contributions
notes: The linked community policy (docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/community/ai_policy.html) allows AI help with full responsibility and suggests an Assisted-by line. It is a rule for contributors, not a statement of how the docs team writes. README and CONTRIBUTING.md are silent on AI.
Command reference pages say they were 'automatically generated from choco --help', which is not AI. Root has README only (no CONTRIBUTING, AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md).
A 2026 blog post describes LLM-made question-answer pairs used to test the docs chatbot, not to write docs. No public docs source (no edit link; feedback goes to ideas.digitalocean.com).
Docs have AI search and chat; some pages carry a machine-built cross-link map. No statement on AI writing. No public docs source (no edit link).

statement_quote: The docs team are huge fans of AI tools like Claude Code and use them to generate content all the time.
contributor_rule_quote: Note AI tool usage in your pull request description using the AI assistance section in the PR template.
notes: README note 'AI and content quality' continues that the team will 'always rely on human review'. Found by the vendor search and in the docs repo; it is not on docs.datadoghq.com itself. The docs site's 'Ask AI' label covers chatbot answers only.
The 'AI-generated content disclaimer' on docs.netlify.com covers Ask Netlify chatbot answers, not the docs. No public docs source (no edit link; github.com/netlify/docs is 404).

contributor_rule_quote: If you write with an agent, use our AI agent skills for docs authoring
notes: Borderline: apps/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md sets out agent skills for writing, editing and reviewing docs and asks for human review. It tells contributors how to write with agents but does not say whether or how Supabase's own docs are written with AI, so it is coded a contributor rule.
AI disclaimers on Dev Center cover the Managed Inference product's output. No public docs source (no edit link).
No public docs source: splunk/public-o11y-docs was archived on 2025-09-02 and writers now work in a private mirror. Search results cover AI Assistant features only.
README and CONTRIBUTING.md never mention AI; no AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md. AI disclaimers on docs cover New Relic AI answers.
No public docs source found (no edit link; github.com/railwayapp/docs is 404).

statement_quote: Portions of IBM Cloud documentation may be generated with the assistance of IBM AI technologies.
notes: IBM Cloud Notices page, last updated 2026-10-26; source terms-of-use/notices.md in ibm-cloud-docs/overview. A blanket notice for the whole docs site, not a per-page label. The overview repo's README is silent on AI.
README, CONTRIBUTING.md and agents.md never say how AI is used; agents.md says 'English is translated from Russian' without saying by whom.
